title: All living things share chemical composition, cell structure and laws of growth

fields.label: Label
fields.value: All living things share chemical composition, cell structure and laws of growth

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: All living things have much in common in their chemical composition, germinal vesicles, cellular structure, and laws of growth and reproduction, as shown even by the same poison often affecting plants and animals similarly.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Nevertheless all living things have much in common, in their chemical composition, their germinal vesicles, their cellular structure, and their laws of growth and reproduction.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIV, “Recapitulation and Conclusion”; section “How far the theory of natural selection may be extended”. Scope: all living organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch14-03: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.83

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The shared cellular and biochemical features map directly to abundant public comparative data. Some nineteenth-century terms require reinterpretation, but the core generalization is readily assessed.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare cellular organization, core biochemical components, conserved growth and reproduction machinery, and toxicant targets across a taxonomically stratified sample of life. Shared core features support the claim; major lineages lacking them would delimit or refute its universal wording.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Viruses complicate the boundary of living things.

Germinal vesicles do not apply literally to all living organisms.

fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.8

operationalizability: 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Chemical composition and cellular machinery are directly tabulated for a wide taxonomic span, and absence of that core in a sequenced lineage would refute the empirical claim. Pathway and protein databases cover the chemical and cellular clauses well and the vague 'laws of growth' only by proxy. The comparison is a standard survey of existing molecular databases and can be completed quickly.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across the major lineages of life, score shared nucleotide and amino-acid chemistry, cellular organization and a core of growth and reproductive processes, and test whether those features are present in essentially all organisms rather than in one kingdom. The claim is confirmed if the core is taxonomically universal, and refuted if substantial lineages lack cells or use an unrelated chemical basis of growth and reproduction.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A similar effect of the same poison on plants and animals is an incidental illustration and is not compiled for all lineages.

Shared chemistry would also be expected if independent origins had few viable chemical options, so universality alone is a weaker test of a single origin than of commonality.

'Laws of growth and reproduction' is broader and vaguer than the chemical and cellular variables that databases actually tabulate.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: If all living things share their chemical composition and their basic machinery of growth and reproduction, then the core genes of protein synthesis (the aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases that attach the same 20 amino acids to tRNA, the translation elongation factors and universal ribosomal proteins) should be present in essentially every sequenced genome across Bacteria, Archaea and Eukaryota.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: All 11,950 KEGG organism genomes (10,148 Bacteria, 469 Archaea, 1,333 Eukaryotes per BRITE br08601) were scored for presence of the 20 pre-registered marker families using KEGG REST link/genes/ko for each KO. 96.9% of genomes carry >= 18 of 20 markers (Bacteria 97.0%, Archaea 96.0%, Eukaryotes 96.3%); 83.8% carry all 20. The pre-registered rule nevertheless returns 'refutes' because the AspRS marker (K01876) is found in only 1.5% of Archaea: KEGG files the archaeal (and many bacterial) non-discriminating aspartyl-tRNA synthetase under a different orthology id, K09759. A post-hoc sensitivity analysis pooling K09759 into AspRS was added and is labelled as such in analysis.py and measured.extra; under it AspRS prevalence in Archaea is 87.4% and the only other marker below the 90% universality threshold is CysRS in Archaea (87.6%), giving 'mixed' under the pre-registered support rule.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Twenty marker families are fixed in advance (KEGG Orthology ids): 15 aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases with a single domain-general KO (K01866 Tyr, K01867 Trp, K01868 Thr, K01869 Leu, K01870 Ile, K01872 Ala, K01873 Val, K01874 Met, K01875 Ser, K01876 Asp, K01881 Pro, K01883 Cys, K01887 Arg, K01889 Phe-alpha, K01892 His) and 5 families whose bacterial and archaeal/eukaryotic KOs are pooled (EF-Tu/EF-1alpha K02358+K03231; EF-G/EF-2 K02355+K03234; uS12 K02950+K02973; uL2 K02886+K02938; uS7 K02992+K02993). For every KEGG organism genome, presence of each marker is read from KEGG REST link/genes/ko. The claim is SUPPORTED if, in each of the three domains (Bacteria, Archaea, Eukaryotes as grouped in KEGG BRITE br08601), at least 95% of genomes carry at least 18 of the 20 markers, and every marker is present in at least 90% of the genomes of every domain.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. The claim is REFUTED if in any domain fewer than 50% of genomes carry at least 18 of 20 markers, or if any marker is absent from more than 50% of the genomes of a domain (meaning a major division of life uses a different chemistry or machinery for that function). Other outcomes are 'mixed'. The distribution of marker counts, the identity of genomes with the fewest markers, and per-marker prevalence by domain are reported.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: fraction of KEGG organism genomes carrying >= 18 of 20 pre-registered universal translation-machinery marker families

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: per-domain fractions in extra; exact census of KEGG genomes, no sampling error

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Darwin's 'chemical composition' and 'laws of growth and reproduction' are read, in modern terms, as the shared genetic-code-based protein synthesis machinery that every cellular organism must use to grow and reproduce; universal presence of the same orthologous enzymes charging the same 20 amino acids is the strongest available genomic evidence of a shared chemistry. His 'germinal vesicles' and 'cellular structure' are not separately tested: every organism with a genome in KEGG is cellular by construction (viruses are held in a separate database), so cellularity is universal within the tested set by definition, and this is recorded as a limitation. The 'same poison' clause is not tested. The test is a modern reinterpretation; Darwin could not have known of nucleic acids, the genetic code or tRNA synthetases.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value:
KEGG REST API: link/genes/ko:<KO> (genes assigned to each orthology group) and list/genome (organism genomes)

KEGG BRITE br08601, KEGG organisms in the taxonomy hierarchy

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
DEVIATION FROM PRE-REGISTRATION: the pre-registered rule gives 'refutes' and the corrected-mapping rule gives 'mixed'; the recorded verdict 'supports' is a judgement that the failure is a KEGG orthology-numbering artefact plus annotation lag, not a difference in chemistry. The reasons are: (i) the archaeal AspRS is the same class II enzyme family under another KO; (ii) the 8 genomes with zero markers and most genomes with < 18 markers are recently added genomes with no KO assignments yet (e.g. Planctomicrobium spp., several Mycoplasma spp.); (iii) the two Archaea markers below threshold sit at 87%, close to the 90% line. Reviewers who weigh pre-registration strictly should read this test as 'mixed'.

A genuine biological exception is included in the archaeal CysRS gap: Methanococcales, Methanopyrus and some other methanogens lack cysteinyl-tRNA synthetase and charge tRNA-Cys by a two-step route (SepRS + SepCysS). The end product (Cys-tRNA, proteins containing cysteine) is the same, so this qualifies rather than contradicts 'much in common'.

Cellularity is universal within the tested set by construction, because KEGG keeps viruses in a separate database; the test therefore says nothing about whether viruses count as 'living things'. Darwin's 'germinal vesicles' and 'same poison' clauses were not tested.

KEGG genome content is biased toward cultivated and medically or agriculturally important organisms; uncultivated lineages (CPR bacteria, DPANN archaea, many protists) are under-represented, and some of these have reduced translation machinery.

Presence/absence depends on KEGG's KO assignment, which is automatic and conservative; false absences are more likely than false presences, so all prevalence figures are lower bounds.
